The campaigns in the south stay limited, and fewer divisions are lost in Serbia and Montenegro. What actually happened: Potiorek's second invasion of Serbia took Belgrade in December 1914 and was thrown back by the Serbian counterattack at the Kolubara, and Potiorek was relieved on 22 December. Montenegro was attacked in January 1916 and Mount Lovcen was taken on 11 January, and the country surrendered within the month. The Serbian army was not destroyed in 1914 and was driven out only in the autumn of 1915, by a combined Austro-German and Bulgarian offensive.
